g.text: MEDIT · Front end — its clients; Modbench is the right column, its client the seam
MODBENCH · The user — in VS Code's trees, panels and palette
MODBENCH · Views — driving adapters: read a value, fire a command
MEDIT · Core — the write side, the read side, the port the front end hears
MODBENCH · Core — one command per gesture, beside the codec of the file it writes; each writes and forgets
MEDIT · Shared kernel — read by both sides and by the adapters
Arrows point the way data moves. Colour is the gesture family; the trace of that name carries the labels.
MODBENCH · Shared kernel — pure; parse and byte-faithful splice, one module per MO2 file

A box talks to the band beneath it, and to the kernel. Change flows up only through a watcher or the notification port. A command writes a file and forgets; the read model beside it learns by watching, and no command reads it: a value it needs arrives as an argument. The two columns meet at the load order snapshot and the stream.
MEDIT · Access — driven adapters; the Index is a view over the two beside it
MODBENCH · Access — the Instance is derived from MO2's files by watching, and nothing else
MODBENCH · Data — systems of record; mEdit is the left column and always running
